$comment: The fixed analysis-quality corpus. Selection criterion, applied before any rate was known for a target and never re-applied afterwards: real-world, actively maintained, server-side TypeScript whose sources form a self-contained subtree that TypeScript can load without installing the repository's dependencies. Every target is pinned by commit SHA and by the git tree object of the measured subtree, so `node scripts/bench-corpus.ts` fails loudly if a checkout drifts. Dependencies are deliberately NOT installed: a call into a package whose types are absent stays unresolved, which moves the measurement in the conservative direction only.

targets.name: hono

targets.name: elysia
targets.what: HTTP server framework with schema-driven handlers

targets.name: drizzle-orm
targets.what: SQL ORM / query builder and database driver bindings
targets.$comment: The repository maps its own `~/*` imports onto `drizzle-orm/src/*` in a tsconfig outside the measured subtree. Reproducing that mapping is corpus setup, not analysis: without it every internal import fails to resolve and the target would measure module resolution rather than contract analysis.
